Mel’s First Year Reflections as a Swiis Foster Carer
items.snippet: Having transferred from another fostering agency, Mel already understood the role of fostering, but her time with Swiis has brought new learning opportunities and rewarding experiences that have made her first year truly special. The post Mel’s First Year Reflections as a Swiis Foster Carer appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
At Swiis, we love celebrating every foster carer’s journey and the milestones they achieve, and Mel, a foster carer from Yorkshire, has recently celebrated her first year fostering with Swiis!

Having transferred from another fostering agency, Mel already understood the role of fostering, but her time with Swiis has brought new learning opportunities and rewarding experiences that have made her first year truly special.

Mel joined Swiis with a young person already in her care, and over the past year, she has also welcomed short-term and respite home finding arrangements. Through this, Mel has provided more young people with a safe and nurturing environment where they can feel heard, supported, and valued.

Mel kindly shared her story with us, reflecting on her journey and experiences during her first year fostering with Swiis.

Looking back on your first year of fostering with Swiis, how would you describe the experience?

“I would describe my first year as positive overall. Both social workers I have worked with have been really good, both very nice and easy to talk to openly, which is very important. Overall, it has been a really good experience!”

Why did you consider Swiis when choosing a fostering agency, and how did you find the transfer process once you decided to make the move?

“Swiis was an agency I had heard of before, and the name stood out to me, which is one of the reasons I chose to foster with them. As I already had a young person in my care, Swiis fit well with both our lifestyles and helped ensure that the young person felt listened to and had a voice.

“I got along really well with the assessor who completed my assessment, and the process felt quick and straightforward. With a previous agency, it took around a year to become a foster carer, but with Swiis, the assessment and transfer process took only a couple of months and felt easy.

“Because I had already been through the process before, I knew what I wanted from an agency. I also knew a few people from my previous agency who had transferred to Swiis, which gave me a good understanding of them. I contacted the recruitment team directly, and because I knew the questions to ask, everything felt very straightforward from the start.”

Can you share the types of support you had during your first year of fostering with Swiis, and how those forms of support made a difference for you?

“I have completed a lot of training in my first year, and there is a lot of training available. I also needed support from the Stability and Support Team during the start of one of my arrangements, and they were great, very helpful and supportive during what was a difficult situation.

“My social workers have always been on hand when I’ve needed them, and overall, the support from Swiis has been very good.”

Can you share a particularly memorable experience from your first year of fostering with Swiis?

“One of the young people I cared for went on to university, which made me incredibly proud. She also came back to visit at Christmas, which was really special as it validates that you are doing something right and shows that they appreciate the care and support you have given them.

“It is important for young people to enjoy their time in care, and when they do, it’s a great feeling. There can sometimes be misconceptions about what being in care is like, often shaped by social media or television, but it can be a warm, loving, and supportive experience that gives young people the opportunities they deserve.

“When a young person comes back to visit when they don’t have to, it’s a real boost and shows they felt happy and supported during their time with you.”

What advice or tips would you give to someone just starting their fostering journey?

“My main advice would be to stay open-minded and avoid having fixed expectations, because every child is different and situations are not always what they seem on paper.

“Fostering can be challenging, so it is important to read all the information you are given, ask questions, and make informed decisions. When you receive a referral, don’t rely only on the written details. Ask more questions, because you cannot fully judge a young person from a short summary.

“If a child has come from an arrangement that broke down, don’t shy away from that. It is not always a reflection of the child, and sometimes it is simply that the dynamic was not right between them and the previous foster carer.

“For example, the older girl I cared for, who is now at university, came to me as an emergency placement and was only meant to stay for a couple of weeks, but she ended up staying for over a year because we had a great dynamic. I didn’t focus on what had happened before; what mattered was how things worked between us, and it turned out really well.

“Don’t pass up the opportunity to care for someone just because things didn’t work out elsewhere. Sometimes personalities and circumstances just don’t match, and that’s okay.”

Mel’s first year with Swiis has been full of memorable moments and shows that being a foster carer can have a truly positive impact, helping to shape a child or young person’s life. If Mel’s story has inspired you to explore fostering, or if you would like to find out more about becoming a foster carer, contact our recruitment team. They will be happy to guide you through the fostering process, explain the support, training, and allowances available, and answer any questions you may have.

items.title: Why More People Than Ever Chose to Foster with Swiis in 2025
items.snippet: 2025 has been an extraordinary year for Swiis, with more people than ever choosing to become foster carers and open their homes and hearts to children in need. The post Why More People Than Ever Chose to Foster with Swiis in 2025 appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
2025 has been an extraordinary year for Swiis, with more people than ever choosing to become foster carers and open their homes and hearts to children in need.

Choosing to become a foster carer is a meaningful step that can shape your life and the children and young people you care for. At Swiis, we are committed to making sure that the journey feels supported and reassuring. From the moment you make your first enquiry and throughout your fostering career, we ensure that foster carers feel appreciated, encouraged, and never on your own.

Ofsted Rated ‘Outstanding’ Across All Areas

We are incredibly proud that every Swiis office is rated ‘Outstanding’ in all areas by Ofsted. Our North East, North West, Midlands and South, and Yorkshire offices all hold this Outstanding rating based on the experiences of children and young people, how well they are supported and protected, and the effectiveness of the Swiis team.

This is a rare achievement within the foster care sector and reflects our unwavering commitment to delivering the highest standards of care and support.

For children and young people, Swiis provide a space where they feel safe, listened to, and supported, giving them the chance to grow and reach goals that may not have been possible otherwise. For foster carers, it means access to expert training and round-the-clock support, ensuring they are never alone on their fostering journey.

North East Ofsted Repot
North West Ofsted Report
Midlands & South Ofsted Report
Yorkshire Ofsted Report

A Trusted Fostering Agency Built on Quality and Care

For over 25 years, Swiis has built a strong reputation as a trusted, independent, family-owned fostering agency. Our long-standing commitment to attaining the best possible outcomes for children and young people is at the core of everything we do.

We have a large number of foster carers who have been with Swiis for many years, reflecting the trust and dedication at the heart of our agency.

Swiis is also highly regarded by our local authority partners. As a Tier One fostering agency, we are among a small number of ‘select’ independent fostering agencies contacted if the Local Authority cannot place a child in-house. This trusted status reflects the confidence placed in Swiis to deliver safe and high-quality care when it matters most.

Supported and Informed from the First Step

Becoming a foster carer is a life-changing decision, and Swiis ensures you are fully informed and supported from your very first enquiry. Whether it is through initial conversations with our recruitment team or attendance at our introductory webinars, you will have access to clear and honest information regarding the fostering role with Swiis and the opportunity to ask any questions you may have.

If you decide you would like to consider fostering with Swiis, you will be offered to attend Day 1 training. This day is designed to share a wealth of information regarding fostering and allows prospective foster carers to learn more about the fostering application process, and is also an opportunity for you to ask any questions you may have. If, following Day 1, you wish to progress to the formal application process, you will be required to take part in 3 further days of training once this has begun.

These further sessions are mandatory and explore children’s behaviour in greater depth and cover the practical and legislative aspects of the fostering role.

“Foster carer input is at the heart of what we do, our courses are written in response to their needs, and their feedback is used to improve the training provision.”

Meet Laura Evans: Training and Development Manager

The assessment is undertaken by an independent qualified social work assessor who will undertake the assessment via a number of planned meetings with you and members of your family in your home. The assessor will provide one-to-one support throughout your assessment, offering advice, reassurance, and guidance at every step.

Expert Post-Approval Training That Builds Confidence

Training at Swiis does not stop once you are an approved foster carer. Within the first eight weeks, foster carers are encouraged to take part in our ‘New Carer Webinar’ programme, which consists of four sessions designed to provide a refresher on key topics. These include managing allegations, dealing with emotions, foster carer well-being and stress management, developmental trauma, and mental health awareness. The webinars are designed to help new foster carers feel confident and supported from the very beginning.

Following these introductory sessions, foster carers take part in mandatory core training throughout their first year, covering regulatory subjects such as child development, safeguarding, culture and diversity, attachment, first aid, managing allegations, and understanding challenging behaviour.

All courses are regularly reviewed and updated annually to ensure they remain current with regulations and best practice, providing carers with the highest standard of training. Depending on the subject, training is completed either annually or every three years, ensuring foster carers’ knowledge and skills stay up to date.

For foster carers working with complex arrangements, children with additional health or disability needs, or parent and child arrangements, specialist training is provided which ensures you feel fully equipped to meet every child’s unique needs with confidence and compassion.

“From the very beginning, Swiis has been an incredible support system. They have listened to me when discussing my choices and have always supported my decisions. I truly believe we work as a team, and I always feel listened to, and I plan to continue fostering with Swiis until I retire.”

Rachel’s Fostering Story

Never Alone on the Journey

All our foster carers are supported by a strong and caring network of professionals. With a range of support services in place, foster carers can feel confident knowing there is always someone to turn to for guidance, reassurance, or practical advice.

Within the first year, every foster carer is paired with a Foster Care Buddy Mentor, an experienced local carer who has been through the fostering journey themselves. They understand how you feel, know what to expect, and can offer personal insights and guidance based on their own experiences, even for the smallest day-to-day questions.

Cate, an approved foster carer with Swiis since 2007, is part of the Buddy Mentor programme and brings her years of experience to support new foster carers. She explains:

“I’ve found we can have really open conversations and I’m also able to reassure them and answer any little questions that come to mind, like the day-to-day things that you don’t need to chat to a social worker about.”

Cate and Becky’s Refer a Friend Success Story

Building a sense of community is central to life at Swiis, and we regularly organise support groups and local activities for foster carers, children, young people, and birth children. These gatherings allow foster carers to share experiences, form friendships, and create lasting memories. They provide encouragement, practical advice, and a reminder that every foster carer is part of a wider supportive network.

Each foster carer also has a dedicated Supervising Social Worker who provides 24/7 support and acts as a direct link between the foster carer, Swiis, and local authorities. They guide foster carers through challenges, celebrate successes, and ensure you always feel equipped to meet the needs of the children in your care.

For children and young people with complex emotional or health needs, Health Advisors offer specialist guidance and ensure carers have access to the training and support they require. Education Advisors also work closely with foster carers and children, liaising with schools and professionals to ensure the child’s needs are understood and fully supported, helping them achieve their potential.

“My role is to provide the foster carer with the appropriate resources to support the children’s learning, depending on their needs and abilities.”

Meet Gareth Thomas: Education Advisor

When additional specialist input or emotional support is needed, our Stability and Support Team is on hand to offer practical strategies, reassurance, and guidance, helping carers navigate even the most challenging situations with confidence.

By combining personal mentorship, professional support, specialist guidance, and a strong community, Swiis ensures foster carers are never isolated and always have the resources, advice, and encouragement they need to succeed.

Experiences Shared by Swiis Foster Carers

The heart of Swiis is its foster carers, and their stories show the real impact of care, community, and support, and why so many choose to stay with us for years.

Lorraine’s Fostering Story

“It is not easy, but with the excellent support from the team at Swiis you will never feel alone, and you will be given the skills to support you in caring for the children you look after.”

Lorraine’s Fostering Story

Jayne’s Fostering Story

“Even if you don’t have all the necessary skills at first, Swiis provides excellent training to support you. All the resources you need are available, and help is always just a call away.”

Jayne’s Fostering Story

More people than ever are choosing Swiis because we combine expert training, care, and unwavering support. Every child deserves a safe and nurturing home, and every foster carer deserves guidance, training, and community. At Swiis, you are never alone, and together we can create brighter futures for children and young people who need it most.

If you are interested in becoming a foster carer, or simply want to learn more about fostering, please get in touch with our team by enquiring here or by calling 0333 577 1234.

The post Why More People Than Ever Chose to Foster with Swiis in 2025 appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.

items.title: Hidden Truths about Fostering
items.snippet: Fostering is incredibly rewarding—but misconceptions often stop people from taking the first step. In this blog, we separate myth from reality, uncover the hidden truths about fostering, and explain what no one tells you about becoming a foster parent, so you can make an informed decision with confidence. The post Hidden Truths about Fostering appeared first on Orange Grove Foster Care.
items.content:
Fostering can be such a rewarding vocation for those who choose to do it. By opening your home to a foster child, you give them a chance to build a better life for themselves, work through their trauma, and live in the caring, loving environment that they deserve. However, many have let themselves be put off looking into fostering because of misconceptions about the profession.

We want to bust some of these myths and take a closer look at the hidden truths about fostering. There’s so much information out there about fostering that it can often be tricky to work out fact from fiction. So what do you need to know about becoming a foster care parent?

We’re going to take a closer look at the truth about fostering and what no one tells you about being a foster parent.

Common myths and misconceptions about fostering

If you’ve thought about fostering but have let yourself be put off by one myth or another, here are 10 facts about foster care that you probably weren’t aware of.

You don’t need to be married to be a foster parent

There’s no need to worry about whether you can foster if you’re a single parent or aren’t married. Here at Orange Grove, we welcome foster parents from all walks of life.

Lots of our amazing foster carers are single, and your marital status won’t impact your ability to become a foster parent. As long as you’ve got a robust support network in place, this shouldn’t be a factor that deters you from fostering.

You don’t need to be wealthy

Don’t let your finances be a factor that puts you off becoming a foster parent. You don’t need to be rich to open your home to foster children, and there’s actually a variety of financial benefits available to foster parents.

As a foster parent, you’ll be entitled to a fostering allowance, as well as tax relief, which will cover the costs incurred from fostering, while also rewarding you for your hard work and dedication.

You’ll also benefit from additional perks, including:

  • Additional payments to celebrate birthdays and religious festivals for each child in your care.
  • Two weeks of paid respite care.
  • A generous mileage allowance for any extra travel involved in caring for a child.
  • Exclusive discounts on our foster parent rewards platform.
  • Up to £3000 for each family you successfully refer to us through our refer-a-friend scheme.

You can still foster if you don’t have parenting experience

Fostering isn’t exclusively available to people who are parents themselves. If you don’t have any direct parenting experience, you could still be a fantastic foster parent, and you’ll probably find that you have a range of transferable skills from other roles you’ve had in the past.

All of our foster parents receive training before they are matched with their first foster child, and we’re proud of the continuing support that we give to our foster parents throughout their fostering journey.

You don’t need to own your own home to foster

If you rent your home rather than own it, this won’t be a barrier to fostering.

You’ll just need to let your landlord know before becoming a foster parent, as fostering means a change in who’s living in the property.

Under the Renters’ Rights Act, landlords can’t refuse tenants simply because they have children or are planning to welcome children into their home, including foster children. That said, there may be some exceptions where restrictions are reasonable and lawful – for example, if the property isn’t suitable due to space, safety, or licensing requirements.

The main requirement is that you have a spare bedroom a foster child can call their own – a safe, comfortable space where they can settle in. You’ll also need enough living space for everyone in your household to live comfortably together. As part of the assessment process, we’ll carry out a home health and safety check too.

It’s not challenging behaviour, it’s trauma

One of the biggest questions you may have about fostering is whether the children you’ll be welcoming into your home will have challenging behaviours.

It’s important to remember that these children have had to deal with a lot of trauma in their young lives and need stability to help them navigate the world. Your job as a foster parent is to build trust and feelings of confidence, and to give these children the loving home that they deserve so that they can go on to live happy, fulfilling lives.

This may be challenging at times, but it will be worthwhile in the end when you can see how you’re helping these children in real time.

You can work and still foster

Many of our foster parents choose to foster alongside other employment. As long as you’ve got the flexibility to do so, it’s more than possible to foster and work.

At Orange Grove, we’ll work with you to make sure that your work schedule fits around the needs of any children in your care. We look at the flexibility of your job, your working hours, your support network, which can help you with childcare or taking foster children to appointments when you can’t, and your health and wellbeing, to make sure that fostering works for you.

You will have input in the foster placements you get

Concerned that you won’t get any choice in the matches you get with fostering? We can happily tell you this isn’t the case at all.

During the matching process, our referrals team will consider your preferences, such as the age range of children you foster, and the type of fostering you provide, before matching you with a child.

If they find a potential match, you’ll get to review all of the information that we have about the child, and the decision will ultimately be down to you.

Don’t be afraid to say no to a match – we want to make sure that it’s the right match for you, your family, and the child.

Fostering is suitable for people of all ages

If you’re worried about your age being a barrier to your fostering journey, then we can put your mind at rest. There’s no upper age limit to who can foster – the minimum requirement is that you are at least 21 years of age.

In fact, if you’re a retired empty nester whose own children have flown the nest, you’re in the perfect position to open your home to a child in need and give them the love and support that they need to flourish.

You can foster if you’re from a diverse background

We champion people from all walks of life to become foster parents. You shouldn’t let the myth that only certain people can foster put you off looking into becoming a foster parent.

At Orange Grove, we celebrate diversity and inclusion, and we want our amazing team of foster parents to reflect the rich, diverse backgrounds that you’ll find throughout the world. That includes LGBT individuals, people from ethnic minority backgrounds, and those who have disabilities.

Fostering can include short-term and long-term placements

One of the little-known facts about fostering is that it doesn’t just involve short-term placements.

In fact, there are lots of different types of fostering that you can undertake, including long-term (from 2 years up to when the child turns 18), disability foster care, respite, emergency, and many more.

So if you think you’d like to become a foster parent but want to welcome a child or siblings into your home for longer, this is something that will be possible.

Start your fostering journey today

Are you curious about fostering and want to know more? Get in touch with one of our friendly advisors today to learn more about the fostering process, what this could mean for you and your family, and how you could transform a child’s life by opening your home to them.

Simply fill out our enquiry form or give us a call on 0800 369 8513 to speak to one of the team and learn more about how you could start your fostering journey today.

items.title: Marion’s Story: Fostering children of different ages while living life to the full
items.snippet: Alongside fostering, Marion is a keen runner and has completed multiple marathons. For Marion, age is just a number. The post Marion’s Story: Fostering children of different ages while living life to the full appeared first on Fosterplus.
items.content:
Marion is 65 and lives a busy, active life. She is a foster parent to children of different ages, has three grown-up birth children, and six grandchildren.

Alongside fostering, Marion is a keen runner and has completed multiple marathons. For Marion, age is just a number. She is kept active and energised by family life, by the children she cares for, and by running, which has become an important way for her to look after her wellbeing and take time for herself.

Making the decision to foster

Marion always knew she wanted to foster, but she also knew it needed to be the right time. Her advice to anyone thinking about fostering is to consider the needs of the whole family. If you have your own children, their needs matter too, and it’s important to feel confident that you can offer time, care and attention to everyone.

Marion began fostering at the age of 54. Before taking that step, she spoke openly with her children and wider family to make sure everyone felt comfortable and involved. Fostering affects the whole household, and while it means sharing time and energy, Marion believes there is more than enough love to go around.

Running for wellbeing and community

Running plays an important role in Marion’s life. It is something she does to stay active and support her mental wellbeing. She started with Parkrun and quickly found a strong sense of community, which she feels has had a hugely positive impact on her life.

Through running, Marion made a close friend, Alison. When Alison decided to run the New York Marathon, Marion suggested they do it together. That decision led to something quite extraordinary.

Since then, Marion and Alison have completed the Marathon Majors, running in Boston, New York, Tokyo, Berlin and London. In August this year, they will run the Sydney Marathon. Once completed, they will be among the first people ever to have finished all seven Marathon Majors.

Fostering with Fosterplus

Marion fosters with Fosterplus and sees her role as offering children consistency, care and the chance to feel safe enough to be themselves. Her hope is that every child who spends time with her and her family can look back and say that their time felt positive and secure.

Marion believes there are many misconceptions about fostering. In her experience, children don’t need extraordinary things. They need time, patience, understanding and care. All children deserve to feel accepted and valued for who they are.

Recently, Marion and her family said goodbye to a much-loved toddler who was able to return to their family. While it was an emotional moment, Marion is grateful for the time they shared and for knowing that the child experienced love and stability while in their care.

Growing and thriving together

At the moment, Marion’s family includes two young people who are an important part of their lives.

Kyle is 12 and full of energy. Marion and her family originally fostered him before becoming his legal guardians through a Special Guardianship Order. Kyle enjoys rugby, is training to be a lifeguard, and volunteers with St John Ambulance. He hopes to become a brain surgeon in the future because he wants to help others. Marion describes him as kind, determined and resilient, and is incredibly proud of the young person he is becoming.

Marion also supports a young man with Down’s syndrome through a Shared Lives arrangement. When he came to live with the family five years ago, he needed a high level of support. Since then, he has made significant progress in his independence and confidence. He now enjoys everyday routines and attended his college prom last year, a moment that meant a great deal to the whole family.

Curious about fostering later in life

Discover everything you need to know from our ‘who can foster’ page.

Who Can Foster

Combining family life and an active lifestyle

One of Marion’s proudest moments came last year when she ran the London Marathon just six days after completing the Boston Marathon, alongside her daughter, who uses a wheelchair, and her grandson. Sharing that experience as a family made it especially meaningful.

Running has become something the whole family enjoys together. Kyle regularly takes part in Parkruns, and Marion now has a cross-country wheelchair so she can take the young man she supports out on running routes. Even her grandson has recently started running.

Marion wants the children in her care to see the value of living a healthy, balanced and happy life. As a family, they find joy in movement, spending time outdoors and being together.

Marion is clear that none of this would be possible without the support of her husband, David. They work as a team and try to make the most of every day. For Marion, fostering alongside family life feels like a privilege and something she is deeply grateful for.

If Marion’s story has made you think about fostering, or if you’d like to learn more about what fostering could look like for you, please get in touch with us today.

5 Tips to Keep Children Safe Online
items.snippet: The internet is a powerful tool, but it can expose children to risks without the right guidance. In this blog, we share 5 essential online safety tips for foster parents to help protect children from inappropriate content, build healthy digital habits, and feel confident navigating the online world together. The post 5 Tips to Keep Children Safe Online appeared first on Fosterplus.
items.content:
The internet can be such a useful tool in everyday life, both for foster parents and for the children in their care. However, it can also be a tricky place to navigate safely and can pose a risk to children who are exposed to age-inappropriate content.  

It can be difficult to know what your children are getting up to online or on social media, but if they have the right practices at their disposal, they can navigate these useful tools safely. Safer Internet Day takes place at the start of each February, exploring different themes to give parents and children tips and tricks for staying safe online.   

To give you everything you need to keep the children in your care safe, we’ve compiled a list of internet safety tips for foster parents.  

Internet Safety Tips for Foster Parents 

 

  1. Open communicationand ground rules 

One of the best tools at your disposal for keeping children safe when using the internet is to encourage open communication, so that they feel they can come to you with any concerns they may have.  

Having ground rules about when, where, and how to use devices will be helpful. Encourage them to use any devices in a communal area so that use of the internet or social media can be safely monitored. Discuss where devices will stay during nighttime and try to keep these in a communal area, too. 

It’s important to have an open and honest conversation to make them aware of their digital footprint. Anything they post publicly online will be available for anyone to see for a long period of time, so motivate them to think twice before sharing anything personal and ensure that they’re using privacy settings to protect themselves. 

  1. Teach them to becautious 

It can be really easy to find and meet new friends in a virtual world, either through websites, social media, or games. But as a foster parent, you’ll want to encourage some basic internet safety to keep your children safe online. 

Discuss with your children that not everyone they meet online will be who they say they are. They could be using photos of someone else or images that have been created using AI to pretend to be someone else, or even AI software to create a realistic-looking filter of someone else entirely when appearing on video chats. 

Discourage them from sharing too much personal information with people they haven’t met, such as photos, addresses, or passwords. It’s always good to make friends, but we should still be wary of sharing too much personal information with them.  

It’s also important to ask permission before sharing photos of real-life friends, too. 

  1. Encourage responsible use of AI

Artificial intelligence has become increasingly popular in recent years, with some children using tools to help them complete homework or even just to play around with. While this can be a great tool for all of us, it’s crucial that we learn to use it responsibly. 

Instead of outright banning the use of AI, discuss with your children how to stay safe while using it. Advise against sharing any personal details, encourage them not to rely on it for absolutely everything, and deter them from secretly using it to finish homework. While that may seem like the easy option in the moment, it’ll mean they have a tougher time learning as they progress through school when topics get more in-depth. 

Discuss with your children that AI isn’t always a reliable source of information. It can sometimes present information about a topic that isn’t correct. Show them what to look out for on devices and websites to see how AI is being used. 

  1. Discuss safe use of social media

If your child is old enough to make use of social media, then it’s important to have an open and honest conversation with them about the stuff they choose to share online and how they use these accounts. 

As we’ve briefly touched on above, privacy settings will be the number one thing to encourage. This can prevent people they don’t know from looking at the content they post online, as well as interacting with them. Anything that they do post publicly, such as names and locations, can be traced back to them.  

Remind them never to add or accept friend requests from people they don’t know, either. You can also show them what to look for if someone is impersonating someone they know, too. 

It can be fun to share photos and video content that they’ve created with family and friends. But as we’ve mentioned above, it’ll be important for them to ask permission first before sharing photos of others. It’s good to be mindful of how the other person would feel if it was shared against their wishes. 

If they see something that makes them uncomfortable or that is unsuitable, foster an open and honest environment with your children so that they feel like they can come to you to discuss it. They can also report or block unwanted content they come across. 

  1. Use parentalcontrol tools 

For younger children, using parental tools can help to improve their online safety. These are offered across all Windows and Mac computers, iOS and Android phones and tablets, as well as gaming consoles. You can use these parental tools to block any unsuitable adult content and set a time limit for how long they can use the devices for to prevent endless doomscrolling. 

For game consoles, you can set time limits, turn off in-game purchases and chat functions, while also restricting the games your children have access to based on their age. Apple devices also have a range of features that you can use for this, too. You can set content and privacy restrictions on your child’s device, prevent any unwanted purchases, and choose which apps they can and can’t download. 

While these tools are useful, they won’t be the whole solution for keeping children safe online. Explain to your foster children that you’re setting up these parental controls so that they can stay safe and that they can always talk to you about why certain settings are set up. Some of these can always change as they grow up, but this should only be at a pace which you deem appropriate for their age. 

What support does Fosterplus offer foster parents? 

Using the above tips can help you to make a start on discussing internet safety with your foster children. But you don’t need to tackle it alone – at Fosterplus, you’ll receive continued support, ensuring you’ve got the knowledge and the tools you need to do a good job. 

You’ll also benefit from our extensive training programme, which includes courses on internet safety, updated regularly to keep up with the ever-changing online world. This includes a mixture of online e-learning, virtual courses, and face-to-face training in our local offices. 

What is Safer Internet Day? 

Safer Internet Day 2026 takes place on 10th February, and this year it’ll be taking a closer look at the safe and responsible use of AI. Artificial Intelligence has boomed in recent years, with popular AI apps and websites becoming a part of daily life for some. Although it can be a very exciting tool to use, it’s important to make safe choices when you do use this technology. 

If you want to know more about Safer Internet Day and the various themes it explores, head over to the Safer Internet website. Or if you want to find out more information on keeping your child safe online, CEOP Education has lots of great resources for you to use. 

Want to know more about fostering? 

If you’ve ever thought about fostering or had questions about why you should foster, our team will be happy to help. The majority of our foster parents often wish they’d started the process sooner! 

Fill out our enquiry form or get in touch via 0800 369 8512 to speak to one of our friendly advisors who can talk to you about the fostering process.

items.title: Meet Wayne Brown: North West Registered Manager
items.snippet: Strong and compassionate leadership, along with consistent and steady support, make this possible, and our Registered Managers play an important role in nurturing that support and maintaining the high standards we are known for. The post Meet Wayne Brown: North West Registered Manager appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
At Swiis Foster Care, our foster carers and the wider team work closely together to care for and improve the lives of children and young people in foster care. Strong and compassionate leadership, along with consistent and steady support, make this possible, and our Registered Managers play an important role in nurturing that support and maintaining the high standards we are known for.

Meet Wayne Brown, our Registered Manager in the North West. He is passionate about supporting foster carers and helping children and young people in care reach their full potential. He loves being part of a team that makes a meaningful difference in their lives every day.

Outside of work, Wayne stays busy by regularly going to the gym, alongside being into music, which is a big part of his life. He is a producer, keyboard player, vocalist, and bass player, and runs his own recording studio. Wayne created a nine-piece band called INNERGROOVE, who have recently released a new single on Spotify!

We spoke to Wayne about the role of Registered Manager, what made him choose fostering, what he loves about his role and his thoughts on what makes a truly great foster carer.

Can you tell us about your journey working within foster care? What experiences have shaped your path, and what motivates you to keep making a difference in this field?

“Growing up, my mum was a foster carer, so I spent my childhood in a home where looked-after children were very much part of the family. That experience inspired me to become a support worker, where I took children out, went to activities, and did focused work with them.

“At the age of 21, I became a foster carer myself alongside working as a support worker. I initially started as a respite carer for my mum before being approved as a full-time foster carer. I did this for three years before focusing more on the support worker role. I later became the regional support manager for the service, and was in this role for 5 years, but then decided I wanted to cast the net and learn more about the wider role, so I was sponsored to complete a social work degree.

“From there, I progressed through roles including supervising social worker, team manager, and registered manager at another organisation with two Outstanding (in all areas) Ofsted inspections under my belt whilst working there. I eventually joined Swiis because I wanted to be part of an organisation where the focus is genuinely on children rather than recruitment or profit. Nearly a year in, I can honestly say that the values, ethics, and morals here are in the right place.”

In what ways have your childhood experiences in a fostering household, along with your own journey as a foster carer, shaped the way you support foster carers today?

“Growing up in a fostering household showed me the variety of children who can come into a home and the different behaviours they can present. It also taught me that what you read on paper is not always what happens in real life. Most of the children my mum looked after brought a sense of fun and energy, but naturally, some of the children presented challenges, which was understandable given their experiences. This insight, in addition to the training I attended, helped me understand the impact of trauma and how that can manifest in their behaviour.

“I often think about new foster carers preparing for their first child coming to live with them. There is excitement, nerves, and lots of questions about what to buy or how to get ready. Things may not go exactly as planned, and that is okay.

“From my own experience as a foster carer, I remember feeling excited about a new child coming to live with me and wanting everything to be perfect. When it didn’t go that way, it was initially deflating, but it taught me the importance of communication. Being kept informed and updated at every step would have made me feel calmer and more prepared.

“That lesson has stayed with me and shapes the way we work at Swiis. It is about keeping foster carers informed, letting them know if things change, and showing respect through open and honest communication.”

Your Role at Swiis Foster Care

Could you share a bit about your role — what it involves and what a typical day tends to look like for you?

“I am the Registered Manager here at Swiis North West, and I have been with the team just under a year. Since joining, there have been a lot of transitions, but together we have built a really strong hub with great energy across the team.

“We recently had an ‘Outstanding’ result in our latest Ofsted inspection in November 2025, which is a true reflection of the team, our wonderful foster carers, and young people. The service was already outstanding when I joined, and since then, we have been able to build on that foundation and are now rated ‘Outstanding’ in all areas.

“Day to day, there are a lot of meetings that I take part in as part of my role. I meet regularly with the Stability and Support team, and I also have weekly catch-ups with the admin team to make sure everyone is on the same page and prepared for the week ahead.

“During the panels, I sit in as the panel advisor, where my role is to provide guidance on Swiis policies and procedures and support the decision-making process.

“Alongside all of this, I produce reports on the service we provide and highlight any issues that arise. That all happens before I even start working directly with the foster carers and the team. As part of my role, I am directly responsible to Ofsted. It is a very dynamic job, and no two days are the same.”

What do you enjoy most about working at Swiis?

“The people and the team! We have a really strong ethos here, and everyone looks out for each other, and there is a great energy across the whole team. The recent ‘Outstanding’ report from Ofsted has really reinforced that. That honesty and willingness to learn is where our real strength lies.”

“I feel it is rewarding sitting in foster carer reviews and panels, listening to the great work our foster carers do, attending activities and getting to know the young people. I try to be as directly involved as possible.”

How do you help your team bring the Swiis values to life in their day‑to‑day work?

“It is about keeping everyone aligned, energised, and engaged, and helping them buy into the vision of what we do, which is ultimately supporting foster carers so they can support children. I am really proud of the team we have. We have fantastic support workers, an amazing Education Advisor, brilliant deputy managers, administrators, and other team members who are centrally based, everyone works together as one.

“It’s a really rewarding environment to be part of, and I couldn’t be happier with the team we have built in the North West.”

During the North West’s recent Outstanding Ofsted inspection, you were praised for going above and beyond in building relationships with children, foster carers, and staff. Could you share some examples of how you did this and the difference you felt it made?

“I think it’s all about building personal relationships, and if you are just sending emails or giving the occasional message, you are not really connecting with people. I make it a point to be in the room with them. I attend activities, support groups, and connect with foster carers and children whenever I can.

“When I first joined, I met with all the North West foster carers, and now, with every new foster carer that joins, I go out with the supervising social worker to see them and to go through their carer agreement and get to know them personally. It is about putting a face to a name and making foster carers feel at ease. I want them to know that I am not just someone who turns up when there is a problem and that I am always at the end of the phone if they need support.

“With the team, we work very much as a collective rather than a hierarchy. If a social worker is busy, I will step in and support with visits or other tasks. I think leading by example is important. I would never ask anyone to do something that I would not be willing to do myself. Showing that mindset helps bring energy and motivation to the team and ultimately supports better outcomes for children and foster carers.”

In your view, what qualities make someone a great foster carer?

“I think a great foster carer is someone who doesn’t take themselves too seriously and doesn’t take things personally, as children can sometimes say things that are not meant in the way they come across. Having a good sense of humour is really important, along with integrity, so if you say you are going to do something, you follow through. Being child-centred and a child-focused advocate, as well as flexible and creative, also plays a huge part in supporting children in the best possible way. In addition to the practical tasks (which are plenty!), keeping on top of training and recording completes the role in my view.”

Wayne’s reflections on fostering and supporting foster carers highlights our commitment to creating positive outcomes for children and young people in care.

By celebrating the teams and individuals who make Swiis exceptional, we aim to demonstrate our dedication to supporting foster carers and the children they care for every step of the way.

items.title: Celebrating a full house of Ofsted ‘Outstanding’ Reports
items.snippet: Following Ofsted inspections across the Midlands and South, North East and North West and with Yorkshire already holding an ‘Ofsted Outstanding’ accreditation, every one of our offices have once again been awarded the highest possible rating of ‘Outstanding’ across all areas of our service. The post Celebrating a full house of Ofsted ‘Outstanding’ Reports appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
2025 has been a truly exceptional year for Swiis Foster Care. After Ofsted inspections across the Midlands and South, North East, North West, and Yorkshire, all of our offices have achieved the highest possible rating of ‘Ofsted Outstanding’ across all areas of our service.

Consistently achieving Ofsted’s highest rating is an exceptional accomplishment within the fostering sector, attained by only a small number of agencies nationwide. Through sustained excellence and unwavering commitment to children and young people, Swiis stands among a select and respected small group of UK fostering providers currently holding multiple ‘Outstanding’ ratings simultaneously.

Ofsted’s inspection report celebrates not only the quality of provision but the life-changing impact of Swiis’s work, noting:

“(Swiis), the independent fostering agency provides highly effective services that consistently exceed the standards of good. The actions of the independent fostering agency contribute to significantly improved outcomes and positive experiences for children and young people.”

What Does Being an Ofsted ‘Outstanding’ Fostering Agency Mean?

Being rated ‘Outstanding’ by Ofsted is more than an impressive achievement. It is a clear indication that children and young people experience the highest quality care and support possible, enabling them to achieve their goals and ambitions that they may not have been able to. It reflects consistently excellent practice, robust safeguarding, and exceptional leadership across every part of our agency.

For the Children and Young People in Our Care

For children, this means they feel safe, valued, and genuinely heard by our foster carers and staff. They are supported to grow in confidence, achieve their goals, and experience the stability and encouragement they need to thrive. It shows that their voices matter and that their wellbeing is at the heart of everything we do.

For Our Foster Carers

For foster carers, this recognition reflects the high-quality training, guidance and round-the-clock support they receive, as well as the positive, lasting difference they make to the lives of the children in their care. Swiis foster carers are among the best in the sector, consistently providing nurturing, stable homes where children and young people feel safe, valued and able to thrive.

Swiis foster carers know they are never alone. They are part of a supportive community, backed by a dedicated team who are always there, listening, guiding and standing alongside them, fully committed to their success and to the wellbeing and future of every child and young person in their care.

As a Fostering Agency

Ofsted only awards ‘Outstanding’ when a fostering agency consistently goes above and beyond for their foster carers and the children within their care. Having consistently ‘Outstanding’ ratings in all areas across our Midlands and South, North East, Yorkshire and North West offices is an exceptionally proud achievement for all Swiis staff.

This accomplishment reflects the dedication, compassion and professionalism of every member of the Swiis team. It is a testament to the hard work our staff put in every day and to our unwavering commitment to achieving the best possible outcomes for children and young people.

Highlights From Our Ofsted Reports

Across the Midlands and South, North East, Yorkshire and North West, children receive nurturing, individualised care that helps them make exceptional progress. Many enjoy long-term, stable home arrangements, building trusting and meaningful relationships with their foster carers.

Below, we have shared just a small selection of the wonderful feedback highlighted by Ofsted. If you would like to explore our reports in full, you can find them on the Government website here:

North East Ofsted Report North West Ofsted Report Midlands & South Ofsted Report Yorkshire Ofsted Report

Support for Children and Young People’s Educational Needs

Education is a key strength, with children attending school regularly, consistently achieving above expectations, and benefiting from specialist support tailored to their individual learning needs. Swiis places strong emphasis on children’s engagement with education, ensuring their commitment and participation are actively supported. Every achievement, big or small, is recognised and celebrated by our teams, helping children build confidence and feel empowered to aspire to and reach their goals.

“Specialist and bespoke support is provided by a dedicated team that works alongside children to break down any barriers to their learning.” – Midlands and South Ofsted Report

“Children’s education and learning progress are at the forefront of the agency’s practice.” – North East Ofsted Report

Swiis Education Advisors work closely with children and foster carers to understand each child’s unique learning needs and provide tailored guidance to overcome challenges. By prioritising education, Swiis ensures that every child and young person has the best possible opportunity to succeed, develop confidence, and achieve their full potential, while foster carers feel fully supported in helping children reach their goals.

Our Dedicated Stability and Support Team

Swiis’s Stability & Support Team provides foster carers with an additional layer of personalised guidance and one-to-one support, helping them respond confidently to any concerns or behaviours a child or young person may present. From the very beginning of their fostering journey, carers can access practical advice and proven strategies to support them through any challenging moments.  The Stability and Support Team can be accessed directly by the foster carer if preferred and is in addition to the exceptional daily support of the social work teams.  This wrap around support ensures foster carers are well equipped to create safe, nurturing environments where children can thrive, grow and overcome barriers they may face.

“Foster carers feel exceptionally well supported and valued by agency staff, which impacts positively on the outcomes of children who are thriving in their foster families.” – North West Ofsted Report

Exceptional Safeguarding

Safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do at Swiis. Children and young people feel safe, supported and valued in our foster homes, cared for by experienced foster carers and supported by highly skilled and committed social work teams. We operate robust and comprehensive safeguarding processes to ensure the highest standards of safety and wellbeing for every child in our care.

Safeguarding is also central to our recruitment, assessment and approval processes. All foster carers and Swiis staff go through rigorous checks and preparation, ensuring they are well trained, confident and fully supported in their role. This strong safeguarding framework promotes stability and enables foster carers to provide safe, nurturing homes where children can thrive.

“Safeguarding children is at the centre of the agency.” – Midlands and South Ofsted Report

At Swiis, every decision and action prioritises the safety and well-being of children. This gives foster carers confidence that they are fully supported when protecting children, knowing they are not alone in ensuring the highest standards of care. Children, in turn, feel secure, protected, and able to build trust with the foster carers caring for them.

“Leaders and managers have an unwavering commitment to safeguarding children and understand the importance of getting it right for children from the start.” – Yorkshire Ofsted Report

Comprehensive and Relevant Training

Swiis provides foster carers with comprehensive and practical training, giving them the knowledge and confidence they need to meet children’s diverse needs. Well-trained foster carers can respond effectively to both every day and complex situations, helping children feel secure, supported, and understood at all times.

“Highly effective post-approval training ensures that foster carers have the relevant skills and knowledge to undertake the fostering role.” – North West Ofsted Report

Child-Focused Leadership and Staff

Swiis is led by experienced leaders who provide strong oversight and inspire continuous improvement. Staff morale is high, workloads are manageable, and teams work closely together to deliver consistent, high-quality care. All regions have strong partnerships with other professionals to ensure children remain at the centre of all practice.

“Foster carers have provided overwhelmingly positive feedback about the support they receive from the agency.” – Midlands and South Ofsted Report

“This agency is led by a team of leaders and managers who have a shared vision and work cohesively to promote excellent outcomes for children.” – Yorkshire Ofsted Report

Foster carers consistently report feeling valued, supported, and heard. This strengthens fostering home-finding arrangements, enabling children to thrive in stable, nurturing homes where their emotional and developmental needs are met.

“Staff morale is high, and staff say that they love their job.” – North East Ofsted Report

Motivated and passionate staff ensure children receive consistent, high-quality care. When staff feel proud and inspired by their work, it directly benefits foster carers and children, creating a supportive environment where everyone can flourish.

“Social workers have manageable caseloads and are in weekly contact with their foster carers.” – North West Ofsted Report

Regular, meaningful contact allows social workers to provide timely guidance, reassurance, and practical support. This ensures foster carers are equipped to meet children’s needs effectively, helping children feel safe, cared for, and supported at every stage of their fostering journey.

A Huge Thank You!

We would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to our foster carers, the children, and young people in our care, and every member of the Swiis team. Your dedication, commitment, and collaboration are at the heart of these ‘Outstanding’ achievements. These Ofsted results celebrate the care, passion, and teamwork that make Swiis a truly exceptional fostering service.

The post Celebrating a full house of Ofsted  ‘Outstanding’ Reports appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.

items.title: Swiis Foster Care: Highlights of an Extraordinary 2025
items.snippet: 2025 has been a year where children have thrived, foster carers have felt truly supported, and our teams have gone above and beyond to deliver life-changing care. The post Swiis Foster Care: Highlights of an Extraordinary 2025 appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
2025 has been a truly remarkable year for Swiis Foster Care, a year defined by commitment, compassion, and collective excellence. Above all else, it has been a year where children have thrived, foster carers have felt truly supported, and our teams have gone above and beyond to deliver life-changing care.

A Landmark Year: Ofsted Outstanding – Three Times Over

The pinnacle of 2025 came in the latter part of the year, when Swiis Foster Care achieved an exceptional milestone: three Ofsted inspections, each awarded Outstanding across all areas. This achievement means that all Swiis regions, including Yorkshire, the North East, the North West, the Midlands and South, are officially rated Outstanding, the highest possible recognition across all areas of our service.

These inspections were embraced by every team member as an opportunity to showcase the exceptional work we do together. An Ofsted Outstanding rating is more than an accolade, it is recognition that children are not only safe but flourishing, supported by stable arrangements, highly skilled foster carers, and leadership that is relentless in its pursuit of excellence.

An outstanding award also reflects the fact that our foster carers are exceptionally well trained and supported, with robust safeguarding, strong professional relationships, and a culture of continuous improvement that truly puts children first.

“The independent fostering agency provides highly effective services that consistently exceed the standards of good. The actions of the independent fostering agency contribute to significantly improved outcomes and positive experiences for children and young people.” – Ofsted, 2025

North East Ofsted Report North West Ofsted Report Midlands & South Ofsted Report Yorkshire Ofsted Report

Children Thriving Through Stability and Belonging

At the heart of everything we do are our children, and this year, their achievements have been nothing short of inspiring. Across Swiis Foster Care, children have experienced increased stability, improved emotional well-being, and the confidence that comes from feeling safe, valued, and listened to.

Many of our children have made significant personal progress, overcoming early trauma with the help of consistent, nurturing foster arrangements. These achievements, whether it’s improved school attendance, renewed self-belief, learning new skills or simply learning to trust again, are powerful reminders of the impact that exceptional foster care can have on a child’s life.

Foster Carers: The Beating Heart of Swiis Foster Care

In 2025, Swiis Foster Care truly demonstrated that we are the agency of choice. We recruited the highest number of foster carers in our history, far exceeding the average for fostering agencies nationally. This extraordinary achievement reflects the trust carers place in Swiis and the reputation we have built for outstanding support, training, and care.

Our foster carers continue to show unwavering dedication, opening their hearts and homes to children who need them most. Their resilience, compassion, and commitment underpin every success we celebrate.

Support That Never Sleeps: 24/7, Every Day

At Swiis Foster Care, support doesn’t stop at office hours. Our foster carers have access to guidance and reassurance 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, ensuring that no concern, challenge, or unexpected situation is faced alone. This constant availability provides confidence, reassurance, and peace of mind, a cornerstone of our outstanding practice.

Rachel’s Fostering Story

“From the very beginning, Swiis has been an incredible support system. They have listened to me when discussing my choices and have always supported my decisions. I truly believe we work as a team, and I always feel listened to, and I plan to continue fostering with Swiis until I retire.”

Read Rachel’s Fostering Story

Bianca’s Fostering Story

“Swiis Foster Care have supported us every step of the way. The assessment process and initial training were both realistic and supportive, and we have made positive relationships with all the Swiis staff. What makes Swiis different is that the teams are genuinely interested in carers and the children, and that makes a big difference.”

Read Bianca’s Fostering Story

Going Beyond: The Stability and Support Team

A few years ago, Swiis Foster Care took an innovative step to further enhance support by developing a specialist Stability and Support Team. Their role is to work directly with foster carers, offering tailored advice, practical strategies, and specialist guidance around behaviours and complex needs.

In 2025, this team had its busiest year yet. Demand grew as carers increasingly accessed this invaluable support, a clear testament to how impactful and trusted the service has become. In response, we expanded the team to ensure every foster carer receives timely, expert help when they need it most.

The team also introduced specialist forum groups and topical webinar training, with subjects chosen by our foster carers themselves. This collaborative approach has empowered carers, strengthened peer connections, and further enhanced the quality of care provided to children.

View The Stability & Support Team

Looking Ahead to 2026

As we reflect on 2025, we do so with immense pride. This was a year of outstanding achievement, heartfelt dedication, and genuine transformation for children, foster carers, and staff alike.

Together, we have shown what is possible when care, expertise, and passion come together. And as we look to the future, one thing remains certain: Swiis Foster Care will continue to go above and beyond, because every child deserves nothing less.

As we move into 2026, our commitment remains unwavering. At Swiis Foster Care, we will continue to evolve and strengthen the support we provide to both our foster carers and the children and young people in their care. Everything we do is guided by one clear purpose: ensuring that every child can feel safe, nurtured, and supported to achieve their full potential.

For those choosing to begin their fostering journey with Swiis, we are committed to making that experience as supportive, flexible, and stress-free as possible. From the very first conversation, through assessment, approval, and beyond, our focus is on supporting our carers every step of the way.

During the next few months, we will be sharing more about the wonderful achievements of our children, celebrating their progress, resilience, and successes. We will also be highlighting the vital role of our social work teams and our foster carers, alongside the specialist provision offered by our Stability and Support Team, giving greater insight into how this enhanced support continues to make a meaningful difference for carers and children alike.

In addition, we will be sharing more details about the feedback from our Ofsted Outstanding inspection outcomes, helping to demonstrate what outstanding practice looks like and how it directly benefits the children we support.

items.title: The New Year’s Resolution That Will Change a Child’s Life
items.snippet: Before you choose a New Year's Resolution like finding a new hobby or improving your health, why not consider making a New Year’s Resolution that will help others and change lives? The post The New Year’s Resolution That Will Change a Child’s Life appeared first on Orange Grove Foster Care.
items.content:
The start of a new year is the perfect time to try something new. Whether that’s finding a new hobby, starting a new job, or committing to new habits that will improve your health and wellbeing. But have you ever considered making a New Year’s Resolution that will help others?

Some of the best resolutions are those that have a profound impact on the lives of others. This could be things like volunteering at your local homeless shelter, raising money for a cause close to your heart, or perhaps even deciding to become a foster parent.

Resolutions that are centred around helping others are often the ones that we’re most motivated to succeed in. They also happen to be the ones that bring us the most joy, purpose and fulfilment.

As a fostering agency, we see firsthand the extraordinary difference foster parents can make to the lives of vulnerable children. It can also be such a rewarding experience for foster families and their children too. So, if you’ve been thinking about fostering for some time, then why not make 2026 the year you apply to become a foster parent? You might just change a child’s life.

4 reasons to make fostering your New Year’s resolution

If you’re still unsure whether to take your first step towards looking after children, then here are 4 more reasons why deciding to start your fostering journey might just be the best New Year’s Resolution you’ll ever make…

1. Change a Child’s World

There are over 80,000 children in care in England. Many of these children will have been through things that no child should ever have to experience. Whether that’s physical abuse, being left to fend for themselves, or losing a parent. Becoming a foster parent and giving a child in care all the love, nurture and support they need will help make an extraordinary difference to their future.

Plus, there are so many different ways that you can help look after children. You may wish to start by offering short-term foster care to children, which means you will be in a child’s life for up to two years. This is often while they’re going through court proceedings, which can be an incredibly turbulent and distressing time.

Or you may want to be a long-term foster parent, where you welcome a child into your home for many years until they turn 18. This is a completely different experience of fostering, where a child can truly become part of your family. Often, the bonds developed over these years continue into adulthood too.

All types of fostering can be incredibly rewarding, and whichever path you choose, you really can change a child’s world.

2. Fostering Can Be Great Fun

While there will be challenging days when you foster – like raising any child – there will also be so many great times that you’ll share together.

As a foster parent, you’ll help children in your care experience the childhood they deserve – and this can be a lot of fun. Whether it’s taking them on their first holiday, watching them take to the stage at the school panto, or singing and dancing to their favourite songs in the kitchen while you’re preparing dinner. Children bring so much joy and laughter to our lives, and you can do the same for them.

3. Provide Stability When They Need It the Most

If you stop to think about it, children in foster care are there with you because they can’t be with their parents right now – perhaps ever. They’ve already seen some of the worst that life has to throw at them and often feel all alone in a world that is crumbling down around them.

You can help them to feel less isolated as they navigate the world around them, and it may not be as difficult as you think. Sometimes all it takes is just being there, just showing them that you are not going anywhere. That sense of stability is what they need most and can really make a difference to children in foster care.

4. The Application Process is a Journey, Not a Commitment

Remember, just by taking that first step to learn more about fostering doesn’t mean you’re committed. The fostering application process is a journey that will help you discover whether fostering is right for you and, if you’re right for fostering.

Plus, at Orange Grove, we will always move at a pace that’s right for you. You will never feel pressured to move to the next stage if you don’t feel ready.

We are committed to providing the training and support that you need throughout the entire fostering process, from in person training to e-learning. You will also have an experienced team around you to give you and your family all the support that you need at each step of your journey.

Start your fostering journey here

Download our brochure and discover everything you need to know about fostering with Orange Grove.

DOWNLOAD GUIDE

Are You Ready to Take Your First Step in 2026?

“We wish we started fostering sooner,” is something we hear our foster parents say all the time. Our message to anyone considering fostering would be not to wait for the ‘perfect time’ to start. If you adore children and have the time, space and energy to commit to making a difference, then make 2026 the year you start your fostering journey.

And in case you hadn’t thought of it, becoming a foster parent will change your life as well as the children in your care. Once you welcome a child into your home, you almost always gain a better appreciation for all the things you do have and are able to do.

Maybe this year we can resolve to be there for a child. After all, it only takes one child at a time to make a real difference, and that’s a resolution worth keeping.

items.title: Let’s Talk About Fostering – a new podcast sharing real stories.
items.snippet: Honest conversations with real foster parents, care leavers and experts from the Polaris Community. The post Let’s Talk About Fostering – a new podcast sharing real stories. appeared first on Orange Grove Foster Care.
items.content:
We’ve launched a brand-new podcast called Let’s Talk About Fostering, and it’s all about real people sharing real experiences of fostering.

Hosted by Faye, the podcast brings together voices from across the Polaris Community to have open, honest conversations about fostering life. From the highs and the challenges to the moments that stay with you forever, nothing’s off limits.

You can listen to Let’s Talk About Fostering on:

  • YouTube

  • Spotify

  • Apple Podcasts

  • Amazon Music

Listen now – three episodes are available

Real voices. Real experiences.

In the opening episodes, you’ll hear from people who know fostering inside out, including:

  • Jo August, CEO, who grew up in a fostering family and has over 35 years’ experience in the sector
  • Alison and Theresa, foster parents sharing what fostering has meant for them and their families
  • Jim McGarrigle, Responsible Individual across several fostering services including Orange Grove, offering a professional perspective shaped by years of experience

Each conversation is grounded in real life, helping paint an honest picture of what fostering is really like.

What’s covered in the podcast?

  • The episodes explore topics such as:
  • What day-to-day fostering really looks like
  • Common myths and misconceptions
  • The support foster parents need — and deserve
  • Experiences from people who grew up in fostering, care-experienced colleagues and long-term foster parents

Is this podcast for you?

You might enjoy Let’s Talk About Fostering if you’re:

  • Thinking about fostering but not sure where to start
  • Exploring whether fostering could fit around your family life
  • Looking for reassurance from people who truly understand the journey

It’s designed to help you listen, reflect and build confidence — at your own pace.

Start listening today

  1. Listen to the episodes available now

  2. Follow or subscribe to catch new episodes, released monthly

  3. Share the podcast to help more people learn about fostering

When open conversations happen, more people feel confident to take the first step — and more children can experience the stability of a supportive family home.
